title: Rapid restoration sprint and executive briefing playbook
author: Daniel Park
body:
Overview
========
This playbook prescribes a fast, repeatable restoration sprint for high-severity incidents that threaten customer-facing SLOs. It pairs a concise operational runbook with editable customer and executive briefing templates so responders can restore service quickly and keep stakeholders informed. Use this document when an incident meets the triggers in the "Incident triggers" section.

Scope and objectives
--------------------
- Scope: multi-region and single-region outages that degrade availability or latency for production API endpoints, embedding pipelines, or orchestration (includes model-serving, KV cache failures, and severe throttling events).
- Primary objectives:
  1. Restore service to SLO-compliant behavior within the sprint window (target: 4 hours for Severity 1, 8 hours for complex distributed degradations).
  2. Provide timely, accurate customer and executive communications.
  3. Preserve forensic evidence for postmortem and compliance.

Incident triggers (automatic and manual)
--------------------------------------
- Automatic triggers (observability):
  - Availability SLO breach > 5 minutes for 5%+ of production requests.
  - p99 latency > 3x baseline for 15+ minutes.
  - Error rate spike >= 10x baseline AND spike sustained for >= 5 minutes.
- Manual triggers:
  - Customer-reported outage impacting >1 top-tier customer.
  - Business judgement by on-call after failed mitigation attempts.

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Incident Lead (IL): owns timeline, channel coordination, and final decisions. Usually the on-call SRE.
- Restore Lead (RL): technical lead for the restore sprint; orchestrates rollback, capacity actions, failovers.
- Customer Liaison (CL): drafts customer status updates and liaises with CSMs.
- Executive Liaison (EL): prepares executive briefings and coordinates with CEO/COO as required.
- Triage Engineers: first responders who collect evidence and apply hotfixes.
- Forensics Owner: ensures logs/traces and artifacts are archived for the postmortem.

On-call escalation matrix (condensed)
-------------------------------------
- Severity classification:
  - Sev 1: major outage, >10% customers impacted or total service failure (page IL + SRE lead + Eng manager).
  - Sev 2: partial outage or major performance regression (page IL + triage + product PM).
- Escalation steps:
  1. Pager triggers on-call IL (0 minutes).
  2. IL acknowledges (target: 2 minutes) and opens incident channel.
  3. If unresolved at 10 minutes, IL escalates to Restore Lead and Eng manager.
  4. If unresolved at 60 minutes, page exec liaison and customer success for external comms.

Minutes-first procedure (timeline with responsibilities)
------------------------------------------------------
1) 0-10 minutes — Acknowledge & Stabilize
   - IL: confirm alert and severity; open channel (Slack #incident-<id> and Zoom if needed).
   - Triage: collect initial evidence: request IDs, trace URLs, recent deploys, config changes.
   - Short checklist:
     - Confirm symptom: availability/latency/errors.
     - Identify blast radius: regions, tenants, model versions.
     - Apply safe mitigation (rate-limit, traffic-shift, kill faulty process).
2) 10-60 minutes — Contain & Assess
   - RL: assemble restore squad and map components in failure path.
   - Forensics Owner: snapshot relevant logs and attach to incident artifacts (S3 path).
   - CL: draft initial customer notice (see templates).
   - If mitigation unsuccessful, prepare rollback or failover plan (PR, infra actions ready).
3) 60-240 minutes — Restore Sprint (iterative 30-minute cycles)
   - RL runs restore cycles: hypothesize, test in canary, promote, validate.
   - Use continuous verification: synthetic checks, internal user smoke tests, and token-level latency samples.
   - Track progress on incident timeline and update status page every 30 minutes minimum.
4) 4-72 hours — Post-restore verification and postmortem kickoff
   - Ensure metrics have returned to baseline for minimum 24-hour sliding window.
   - Forensics Owner runs artifact integrity checks and hands off evidence to PM for postmortem.

Restore decision criteria (quick reference)
-----------------------------------------
- Promote canary when:
  - 0 errors on canary pod for 30 minutes AND
  - p95 latency within 1.5x baseline for canary traffic.
- Rollback when:
  - Error rate increases by >3x after promotion or
  - Latency degrades customer SLOs for 15+ minutes post-change.

Quick-access runbook table (dashboards, commands, and artifacts)
----------------------------------------------------------------
| Purpose | Dashboard / Command | Owner |
|---------|---------------------|-------|
| Top-level availability | https://grafana.redwood.com/d/availability | IL |
| Recent deploys | git log --since='6h' services/serving | Triage |
| Kill runaway process | kubectl -n prod delete pod <pod> | Restore Lead |
| Shift traffic to failover region | ./ops traffic-shift --to=us-west-2 | Restore Lead |
| Collect traces for request | curl "${TRACE_API}/trace?req_id=<id>" > /tmp/trace.json | Forensics |
| Archive artifacts | aws s3 cp /tmp/trace.json s3://incidents/<id>/trace.json | Forensics |

Communication templates (fill-in placeholders)
---------------------------------------------
- Initial customer notification (quick canvas):
  Subject: [Incident] Service disruption impacting X - initial notice
  Body: We are investigating a degradation affecting the Redwood Inference API impacting customer requests to <service/component>. Impact: <brief impact summary>. Current action: <mitigation applied>. Next update: <T+30m>. Contact: <CSM email>.

- 30-minute status update (public status page / customer-facing):
  Status: Investigating
  Summary: We have identified increased latency/errors for <component>. Scope: <regions/tenants>. What we're doing: <list of actions>. ETA: <best estimate>.

- Resolution notice:
  Status: Resolved
  Summary: Root cause: <short cause>. Resolution steps: <what was done>. Post-incident action: <next steps and ETA for postmortem>. Credits: SLA credits will be evaluated per contract.

- Executive briefing (one-page) template:
  - Title: Executive incident brief — <date> — Incident <id>
  - Impact summary: <number of customers affected>, <duration>, <key metrics (p99, error-rate)>
  - Timeline: important timestamps (detection, mitigation, restore)
  - Root cause hypothesis and evidence: <summary>
  - Business impact: revenue, support load, contractual exposure
  - Remediation & prevention: short-term and long-term actions with owners and ETA

Preservation and evidence checklist
----------------------------------
- Create incident S3 bucket: s3://incidents/<id>/ with enforced retention policy.
- Export relevant DB queries, trace samples, and core dumps.
- Tag traces with incident id and store APM snapshots.

Game day and exercise guidance
-----------------------------
- Frequency: quarterly full-day game day, monthly 2-hour tabletop for critical subsystems.
- Example simulation: KV cache mass eviction leading to p99 spikes and throttling across serving fleet.
- Scoring rubric: time-to-detect (30%), time-to-restore (40%), quality of comms (15%), evidence completeness (15%).
- Post-sim: quick retro (30 minutes) and action items with owners assigned in JIRA.

On-call rotation and handoffs (practical rules)
----------------------------------------------
- On-call primary acknowledges within 2 minutes and maintains responsibility until formal handoff.
- Handoffs must include: incident state, outstanding actions, next scheduled update, and outstanding risks.
- Shadowing policy: new responders shadow for 4 incidents before taking solo on-call for sev1s.

Runbook maintenance and governance
---------------------------------
- Runbooks must have an owner and quarterly review date listed in the incident index.
- After every Sev1, the IL schedules a postmortem within 7 business days and assigns action owners.
- Retire obsolete steps via PR and link to test evidence from game days.

Appendix: handy CLI snippets and example commands
------------------------------------------------
- Traffic shunt (dry-run): ./ops traffic-shift --to=canary --dry-run
- Snapshot p99 over last 60m: curl "https://metrics.redwood.com/query?p99&since=60m&service=serving"
- Archive logs: logs export --service serving --since 2h --out /tmp/serving-logs.tgz && aws s3 cp /tmp/serving-logs.tgz s3://incidents/<id>/

-------------------------
